title: Tokenizer boundary telemetry and template resolution during model onboarding
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a robust process for detecting, resolving, and backfilling tokenizer <> chat-template incompatibilities that surface during model onboarding and version pinning. Several recent onboards exhibited subtle token boundary shifts that caused role delimiting and structured output regressions in downstream apps. This ticket establishes telemetry, an "interpreter" reconciliation layer, and an automated backfill pass to keep onboarded profiles stable across runtime and tokenizer updates.

Background / Motivation:
- Tokenizer changes (subtokenization variants, escape handling) sometimes shift message boundaries and delimiter tokens, causing prompt-template mismatches and generation regressions after pinning models or publishing performance profiles.
- Existing onboarding flow runs unit tests and sample prompts but lacks fine-grained token-boundary telemetry and no automatic remediation path for already-pinned profiles.

Goals:
- Surface token-boundary deltas as part of onboarding telemetry (per-model, per-template).
- Provide an interpreter shim that maps legacy template delimiters to canonical token sequences for new models during onboarding, without altering user templates.
- Implement a safe backfill pipeline to re-evaluate pinned model profiles and publish minor patch rollouts when tokenizer-driven regressions are detected.
- Define clear acceptance criteria and rollouts with canary thresholds to avoid user impact.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Onboarding pipeline emits per-template token-boundary diff metrics and a human-readable diagnostic report saved to the model profile.
2) Interpreter shim can be toggled per-model and correctly normalizes 95% of known delimiter variants on our standard template corpus.
3) Backfill workflow can run against dedicated capacity with a job summary (pass/fail, diff counts) and a safe publish path requiring PM+Eng approval.
4) Existing pinned profiles have a documented remediation path; at least one legacy profile is backfilled in staging and validated.

Proposed approach:
- Telemetry: Add tokenizer boundary hash and token-diff histogram to onboarding artifacts. Emit per-template examples where boundary alignment changes exceed threshold. Store diffs in the model profile metadata.
- Interpreter shim: Implement a small, pluggable layer in the onboarding harness that maps common delimiter markers (role markers, suffix/prefix tokens) to a canonical token sequence. The shim runs only during onboarding and in the backfill job; it logs mappings and confidence scores.
- Backfill pipeline: A scheduled job (manual trigger for high-risk) that runs the onboarding harness against pinned profiles with the new tokenizer. The job produces a summary report and optional patch publish that updates the published profile with a compatibility note.
- Rollout/controls: Feature flags per-org and per-model, canary on 5% of traffic, automatic rollback if SLI degradation detected.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for token-diff generation and interpreter normalizations.
- Golden prompt set regression suite across 200 canonical templates.
- Staging backfill run against 3 representative customer profiles; validate structured output and sample QA prompts.
- Load test the backfill job to ensure dedicated capacity handles it without impacting runtime SLOs.

Metrics / Observability:
- New metrics: tokenizer_boundary_changes.count, template_alignment_failures.count, interpreter_confidence.avg, backfill_patch_rate.count.
- Dashboards: onboarding telemetry dashboard with per-model heatmap and template-level examples.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement telemetry and storage only (no interpreter) — ship as opt-in for a week.
2) Deploy interpreter shim behind feature flag and run in "dry-run" mode for two weeks.
3) Enable backfill job in staging; run against pinned profiles.
4) Canary publish to 5% of customers with rollback hooks.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives: tune thresholds and include manual approval for publish.
- Runtime overhead: keep interpreter isolated to onboarding/backfill jobs; do not add to production request path.
- Customer surprise: include change notes in profile metadata and notify Solution/CS teams for any backfill that modifies published behavior.

Docs / Links:
- Design note: https://docs.redwood/team/onboarding/token-boundary-design (internal)
- Golden prompt corpus: drive.google.com/golden-prompt-corpus (internal)
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
